Restrict the effective Site offering to supported member or member,spouse applicants. applicant=member hides the Eligibility dependent question and spouse/child availability rows. applicant=member,spouse hides Child from Eligibility and child availability rows. Coverage Information retains the allowed applicant amount rows independently of form choices. Product controls, applicable sections, cart, preview and Receipt honor the same restriction. The URL never enables people/products absent from Site assignments. Site-scoped entry context persists across routes and resume; a new category/product campaign without applicant clears an older applicant restriction. Unsupported values clear the URL restriction while retaining Site/product limits.

urlParameters.sourceReference: Global Coverage URL review November 16, 2026; shared runtime and confirmed user decisions
urlParameters.behavior: Restricts the effective Site offering to the listed categories, including comma-separated categories. categories is an equivalent alias. If both names are supplied, category takes precedence, including an empty value. Values are trimmed and case-insensitive; all clears the category restriction. Unknown or empty category scope offers no matching products rather than expanding the offering. Product and applicant restrictions still intersect. Both names start a new category campaign and clear omitted previous campaign controls. Saved entry context uses the canonical category key and persists across routes and resume.

urlParameters.sourceReference: Global Coverage URL review November 16, 2026; shared runtime and confirmed user decisions
urlParameters.behavior: Equivalent alias of category, including comma-separated values, all, product intersection and campaign reset/persistence. category wins when both names are present, including an empty category. The application stores one canonical category value; this is not a separate Site setting.

urlParameters.sourceReference: Global Coverage URL review November 16, 2026; shared runtime and confirmed user decisions
urlParameters.behavior: Restricts product display throughout the site to assigned products matching the listed G-numbers. Requires a nonempty category or categories parameter on entry. Product/category/applicant scopes intersect; unavailable or malformed IDs never enable products. Multiple G-numbers are comma-separated. A product-only entry cannot reuse a previous campaign category. Saved application scope persists across routes and resume.

urlParameters.sourceReference: Global Coverage URL review November 16, 2026; shared runtime and confirmed user decisions
urlParameters.behavior: Disables the listed products’ Coverage amount dropdowns only when amt supplies one valid, unambiguous, currently permitted positive amount for that product/applicant. Missing, malformed, duplicate or unavailable amt values do not create a URL-driven lock. Fixed child benefits and other applicants validate independently. This does not select coverage, enable products or waive eligibility/amount limits. Explicit Site/product/applicant amount-lock configuration remains independent.

urlParameters.sourceReference: Global Coverage URL review November 16, 2026; shared runtime and confirmed user decisions
urlParameters.behavior: Displays a Featured chip on the listed available product on Coverage and prioritizes that product and its category across shared product/category displays. It takes precedence over firstCategory and configured ordering. It does not enable a product, change eligibility or elect coverage. Unmatched values do not change ordering; campaign presentation persists across routes and resume.

definition.name: Chronic Illness Rider (CIR)
definition.description: Chronic illness coverage from $50,000 to $1,000,000 for members and $25,000 to $1,000,000 for spouses.

applicantDescriptions.member: Chronic illness coverage from $50,000 to $1,000,000 for members.
applicantDescriptions.spouse: Chronic illness coverage from $25,000 to $1,000,000 for spouses.

definition.name: True Own-Specialty Disability Definition Rider
definition.description: Coverage with a true own-specialty definition of disability pays full benefits if you cannot perform the work of your medical specialty even if you are gainfully employed in another occupation.

definition.name: Cost of Living Adjustment (COLA)
definition.description: Provides that on the anniversary of a continuing disability, the monthly benefit for the next 12 months is increased to reflect changes in the CPI-U for the previous 12 months, subject to a maximum increase for a single disability.

definition.name: Catastrophic Disability Benefit
definition.description: Provides additional monthly benefits for certain conditions that require extra care.

definition.name: Accidental Death & Dismemberment
definition.description: If you die as a result of an accident, the life insurance company will double the original death benefit of your policy.

definition.name: Waiver of Premium Rider
definition.description: Waives your premium payments should you become totally disabled before age 60; see brochure/certificate for details.

definition.name: Accidental Death & Dismemberment (AD&D) Rider
definition.description: If you die as a result of an accident, the life insurance company will double the original death benefit of your policy.

definition.name: Chronic Illness Rider (CIR)
definition.description: Accelerate up to 50% of the portion of your life insurance subject to the Chronic Illness Rider should you be permanently unable to perform 2 out of 6 activities of daily living or require substantial care due to permanent cognitive impairment.

definition.name: Automatic Benefit Increase Rider (ABI)
definition.description: Automatic benefit increase of $25,000 per year for up to 10 years, with no additional medical underwriting required. Subject to increased premium due with each annual increase.

definition.name: Chronic Illness Rider (CIR)
definition.description: Accelerate up to 50% of the portion of your life insurance subject to the Chronic Illness Rider should you be permanently unable to perform 2 out of 6 activities of daily living or require substantial care due to permanent cognitive impairment.

definition.name: Outpatient Emergency Room Benefit
definition.description: Optional Dependent Child(ren) Emergency Accident Benefit pays $50 for a covered outpatient accident visit for children under age 19. Limited to two visits per calendar year; includes hospital, ambulatory surgical center, urgent care or private licensed physician's office.

definition.name: Online medical questions + instant decisions
definition.descriptionHtml: Presents health questions on the pages that require them, based on the coverage and underwriting type selected, and returns an instant decision immediately after: Conditionally Approved, Unable to Offer, or Sent for Review. Simplified Issue and Tele-Supplemental (Life and Disability) present questions directly in the application; QuickDecision hands the applicant to a separate underwriting system to answer questions; Guaranteed Issue and non-underwritten products require none. Fully underwritten and Tele-Supplemental applications are always sent for review, even after answering questions online.
definition.impactedAreasHtml: Health question pages (Simplified Issue, Tele-Supplemental Life/Disability, QuickDecision, Chronic Illness Rider) and the Receipt page — determines what health questions an applicant sees and what decision they receive immediately after submitting.

definition.name: Instant quote
definition.descriptionHtml: Lets a prospective or in-progress applicant estimate their premium and coverage amount using a few basic details (date of birth, gender, tobacco use, state, ZIP), without starting or committing to a full application.
definition.impactedAreasHtml: Landing page (primary entry point) and page-helper shortcuts during the application, which reopen the same estimate without losing progress.

definition.name: E-cart
definition.descriptionHtml: Shows the applicant a running summary of every coverage product they've selected, with a per-product cost breakdown and running total, so they always know what they're applying for and what it costs.
definition.impactedAreasHtml: Persistent header icon with a selection-count badge, shown on every application page except Home and after final submission, plus an inline summary on the Coverage page.

definition.name: Monthly/annual rate toggle
definition.descriptionHtml: Lets an applicant switch a displayed estimated premium between a monthly amount and an annual amount, so they can compare cost the way that's meaningful to them.
definition.impactedAreasHtml: Coverage cart and quote tools — affects how an estimated cost is displayed; does not change the actual payment frequency, which is chosen separately on the Payment page.

definition.name: Coverage brochure panel
definition.descriptionHtml: Shows a brief description, amount range, and eligibility (who it's available for) for each coverage category and product, with access to the full brochure/certificate for more detail, plus a QuickDecision callout for products eligible for an instant decision.
definition.impactedAreasHtml: Landing page ("Your coverage options") and the application menu's "About Coverage" option — lets prospective and in-progress applicants explore what's available without starting or interrupting an application.

definition.name: Coverage portfolio
definition.descriptionHtml: Shows an applicant a summary of their existing in-force coverage, grouped by covered person, once their membership has been verified — so they can see what they already have before deciding what else to apply for.
definition.impactedAreasHtml: Coverage page, available after eligibility/membership verification succeeds.

definition.name: Page helpers
definition.descriptionHtml: Gives applicants quick access to contextual help — such as cost estimates, coverage explanations, or process questions — directly from the page they're on, without leaving the application or losing progress.
definition.impactedAreasHtml: Membership, Eligibility, Coverage, Beneficiary, Health, and Payment pages — reduces drop-off caused by needing outside information to answer a question.

definition.name: Advisor-led application
definition.descriptionHtml: Lets a licensed advisor start or continue an application on behalf of an applicant, complete the portions they're permitted to fill in, and hand the application to the applicant to review, complete any remaining sensitive information, and sign.
definition.impactedAreasHtml: Advisor login and hand-off pages, plus Profile and Review, which branch depending on whether an advisor or the applicant is completing them — supports an assisted sales channel alongside direct self-service applications.

definition.name: Abandoned leads
definition.descriptionHtml: Identifies applicants who start an application but don't complete it, so they can be followed up with and given the opportunity to finish.
definition.impactedAreasHtml: Applies across the entire application flow — surfaces incomplete applications for outreach rather than losing them silently.

definition.name: Autosaved application
definition.descriptionHtml: Saves an applicant's progress automatically after they submit the first page of the application, so they don't lose their work if they leave and come back.
definition.impactedAreasHtml: Applies from the first application page onward — removes the need for an applicant to complete an application in one sitting.

definition.name: Reminder emails
definition.descriptionHtml: Sends the applicant email reminders throughout the application process — confirming that progress has been saved, and prompting them to return and finish if their application is left incomplete.
definition.impactedAreasHtml: Sent after key milestones such as progress being saved and applications left pending completion — keeps applicants engaged and reduces abandonment. See Mock Email Preview for example email content.

definition.name: Resume with MFA
definition.descriptionHtml: Lets an applicant return to and continue a previously started application by verifying their identity with their email and phone number.
definition.impactedAreasHtml: Resume entry and verification pages — lets an applicant safely pick up an incomplete application from a new session.

definition.name: TPA integration
definition.descriptionHtml: Matches an applicant against their organization's member roster to verify eligibility and membership, streamlining the application and unlocking access to their existing coverage information.
definition.impactedAreasHtml: Eligibility (verification step) and Coverage (unlocks the coverage portfolio) — reduces manual eligibility entry for members whose group maintains a roster.

definition.name: Online financial questionnaire
definition.descriptionHtml: Collects additional income and net-worth information from an applicant when their requested Disability coverage amount is large enough to require closer underwriting review.
definition.impactedAreasHtml: Profile page — appears only for applicants requesting higher Disability coverage amounts, with additional self-employment detail collected when applicable.

definition.name: Optional online payment
definition.descriptionHtml: Lets an applicant provide payment information as part of the application, or skip it, depending on what's configured for their organization. When collected, payment isn't charged unless and until the application is approved.
definition.impactedAreasHtml: Payment page — can be configured as required, optional, or excluded per client, changing whether and how payment is collected during the application.

definition.name: Optional online beneficiary
definition.descriptionHtml: Lets an applicant designate who should receive benefits for the Life/Accidental Death coverage they've selected, or skip it, depending on what's configured for their organization. Supports multiple primary and contingent beneficiaries, individuals or trusts.
definition.impactedAreasHtml: Beneficiary page — appears only for applicable Life/AD products, and can be configured as required, optional, or excluded per client.
